rationale: Final iteration, so this candidate should be the best-supported design, not a new experiment. Iteration 10 (sensors at x = ±0.030 m, 16 mm footprints, kp 6.0, kd 0.6, ki 0.05, base_speed 1.2, last_direction) is the best raced design at 125.48. Lowering speed from 1.4 to 1.2 raised the total score and the s-bend progress (0.24 to 0.34), and it lowered the oval steering_oscillation risk. Oval progress fell (0.57 to 0.51), so the speed gain is mixed, but the overall score rose. Iteration 9 showed that widening the sensors to ±0.040 m and raising kp to 8.0 cut progress on both tracks, so I am not carrying that change forward. Oval max_error has stayed at 0.061 to 0.065 across every gain, reach and kd tried, and body_width cannot relax the 0.06 m off-track limit. The untested levers are line_loss search direction and base_speed between 1.2 and 1.4. Both carry a risk of destabilising a design whose score is already the best measured, and with no iteration left after this one, the race result is the only chance to score. I therefore submit the iteration 10 design unchanged, so that the race scores the best measured configuration. Hypotheses to check in the telemetry: (1) speed drives progress on s-bends but costs progress on the oval, so the best base_speed may lie between 1.2 and 1.4; (2) line losses at bend entries (1.3 to 1.7 per run) are the next limit on progress; (3) max_error near 0.064 is set by edge response at the first large offset, not by gain.
